subject: Score instrumentation & action-grid: Asha Mehta debrief
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Score instrumentation & action-grid: Asha Mehta debrief

Hi all,

Quick kick-off for Asha's debrief (SWE frontend candidate). Interview loop finished yesterday; I pulled the draft scorecards and attached my consolidated notes (see scorecard-AshaMehta-20280314.pdf). There is a fair spread across system design and behavior — one interviewer gave a 4/5 on architecture, another a 2/5 citing lack of tradeoff reasoning.

Ask: please paste your final scores into the attached rubric-v2.xlsx by 10:30am PT and call out any must-have concerns in-line. I'm proposing we use an action-grid:
 - Avg score >= 4.0 -> advance to final on-site
 - Avg score 3.0-3.9 -> follow-up technical take-home + manager sync
 - Avg score < 3.0 -> no-go (but provide feedback)

If you disagree with thresholds, flag it here — want alignment before I respond to Sophie at TalentHub.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Hiring Manager, Frontend
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Score instrumentation & action-grid: Asha Mehta debrief

On Wed, 14 Mar 2028 at 08:12, Dylan Brooks wrote:
> Quick kick-off for Asha's debrief...

I uploaded my scores into rubric-v2 (sheet: Marissa). My quick read: system design concern is real but compensating strengths in frontend architecture and ownership. My averages:
 - Technical depth: 3.6
 - System design: 2.8 (asked to clarify tradeoffs, didn’t land)
 - Culture/ownership: 4.5

I lean to the 3.0-3.9 bucket -> follow-up take-home focused on tradeoffs + a short manager sync. If the rest of the panel skews higher, I'm open to advancing, but we should ensure the take-home is tightly scoped.

Attachment: resume-AshaMehta.pdf (from GH).

-Marissa
Senior Eng, Frontend

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Score instrumentation & action-grid: Asha Mehta debrief

Thanks — I entered scores too. I gave a 4.2 on technical depth (good JS patterns, component design) and a 3.0 on system design because while her proposals were product-aware, she didn't quantify latency/complexity tradeoffs.

Proposal: keep Dylan's thresholds but add a secondary check for variance. If score variance across reviewers > 1.0, require a 20min follow-up synchronous problem walk-through (not a take-home) to clarify gap before a decision. That keeps the loop fast and focuses on the exact divergence.

Jonas
Staff SWE, Platform

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Score instrumentation & action-grid: Asha Mehta debrief

Uploading my scores now (rubric-v2.xlsx, sheet: Kimberly). My view: strong code craft and product intuition, but the system design notes matter for a staff-mentored role. My averages: 3.9 overall.

Agree with Jonas on a variance check. Practical next steps I support:
 - Run variance calc in rubric (I added formula in the doc).
 - If variance > 1.0 -> 20min sync with Dylan + short targeted prompt I can host.
 - If avg between 3.0-3.9 and variance <= 1.0 -> take-home + manager sync.

Also flagged an edge-case where interview #3 didn't see the same prompt (candidate was asked a UI performance micro-problem vs others asked architecture). That could explain variance — flagging because it affects fairness.

-Kimberly
Engineering Manager, Frontend

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@talenthub.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Score instrumentation & action-grid: Asha Mehta debrief

Thanks everyone — good convergence. Final call: following the agreed instrumentation:
 - I calculated average = 3.92, variance = 1.05 -> falls into follow-up bucket but variance is > 1.0.
 - Action: schedule a 20-minute sync (behavior + focused architecture dive) with me + Kimberly this Friday. If Asha clarifies tradeoffs satisfactorily, we'll move her to final on-site; otherwise she'll get a targeted take-home with clear acceptance criteria.

Sophie — can you ping Asha for availability Friday 10am–2pm PT? I'll draft the 20min prompt (will keep it focused on tradeoffs and a tiny integration sketch).

Links: Greenhouse candidate (https://greenhouse.io/candidates/gh-4592) and rubric (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c_rubric-v2). Attachments: scorecard-AshaMehta-20280314.pdf.

Dylan
